title: Russia Launches 2 Ballistic Missiles + 122 Shahed Drones at Ukraine Overnight; Kyiv Market Destroyed, 4 Killed — Day 1,552
detail: On the night of May 25–26, 2026 — Day 1,552 of Russia's full-scale invasion — Russian forces launched 2 ballistic missiles and 122 Shahed-type kamikaze drones at Ukraine in a follow-on attack after the May 23–24 mass barrage. Ukrainian air defenses shot down 111 of the 122 drones; the 2 ballistic missiles were not intercepted. In Kyiv, strikes ignited a large fire at one of the capital's oldest market complexes; a subway station used as a civilian shelter was also damaged. At least 4 people were killed and dozens were wounded across Kyiv. In Sumy's Romny district, Russian drone strikes caused fires and injured 3 people. In Mykolaiv, a drone strike damaged an administrative building and two high-rise residential buildings. The wave was part of Russia's sustained aerial campaign — the third successive night of large-scale attacks following the Oreshnik IRBM strike on Bila Tserkva on May 24 and the mass 600-drone/90-missile assault of May 23. The Russian military framed the attacks as retaliation for Ukraine's strike on a facility in occupied Starobilsk (May 22) that Russia claimed killed 21 students.

media.caption: Fire engulfs Kyiv's historic market complex following Russian drone strike overnight May 25–26, 2026

title: Russia Warns All Diplomats and Foreign Nationals to Leave Kyiv Before 'Systematic' Strikes; EU, France, Poland Defy Threat
detail: On May 25–26, 2026, Russia issued an extraordinary public warning — conveyed through Foreign Minister Lavrov and official Kremlin channels — urging all foreign embassies, diplomatic staff, and foreign nationals to evacuate Kyiv immediately before what Moscow called 'systematic and sequential strikes' on the Ukrainian capital. The warning was transmitted directly to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and European counterparts. Russia framed the threat as retaliation for 'continuing terrorist attacks by the Kyiv regime,' referring in particular to Ukraine's May 22 strike in Starobilsk. The threat represented an escalation in psychological warfare: no previous Russian warning had so explicitly targeted the diplomatic community. Western governments rejected the ultimatum outright. The EU, France, Poland, and other NATO delegations publicly stated they would remain in Kyiv; European governments summoned Russian ambassadors to protest; and EU leaders described the threat as a 'sign of desperation.' Ukraine's Foreign Ministry accused Russia of attempting to 'blackmail diplomats' into abandoning Kyiv. By May 26–27, ISW and analysts noted that some Russian officials appeared to be walking back the most extreme formulations of the threat, while strikes continued on Ukrainian cities. The US denied a visa to Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Alexander Alimov, who was expected to attend a UN Security Council session.

media.caption: Russia warns diplomats to leave Kyiv ahead of promised 'systematic strikes'; EU and NATO allies defy threat — May 26, 2026

title: ISW: Ukraine Advances Near Zaporizhzhia and Slovyansk on Day 1,552; Russian Losses Reach ~1,357,900
detail: On May 26, 2026 — Day 1,552 of Russia's full-scale invasion — the Institute for the Study of War (ISW) published its daily assessment noting that Ukrainian forces registered geolocated advances in western Zaporizhzhia Oblast and in the Slovyansk direction, continuing limited offensive pressure despite the ongoing massive Russian aerial campaign. Russia launched 65 attacks against Ukrainian positions across all front sectors. Fighting remained heaviest in the Pokrovsk sector. According to the Ukrainian MoD's daily losses bulletin, Russian cumulative losses reached approximately 1,357,900 personnel as of May 26, with approximately +960 losses recorded over the preceding 24 hours. Equipment losses continued to mount including +1,307 UAVs and +39 artillery systems on May 26. ISW also assessed that Russia and Belarus appear to be setting conditions to potentially justify launching drone strikes on Ukraine from Belarusian territory — a significant potential escalation not seen since the early days of the invasion. Norway pledged approximately $40–42 million to support Ukraine's energy sector rehabilitation on May 26.

media.caption: Russian cumulative losses reach ~1,357,900 personnel on Day 1,552, May 26, 2026 — ISW notes Ukrainian advances near Zaporizhzhia and Slovyansk
